# How Pages lays out fonts of the Mac, as measured on the reference
# machine (DOC-05). Desk lays a family out this way whatever font stands
# for it, so its lines are as tall and as wide as in Pages.
# ascent, descent and leading are in ems: the leading is the space added
# to each line. "above" puts the leading over the text, as Pages does with
# Apple's own fonts, which have no line gap: their leading is a fifth of
# their height. "below" puts it under the text, as with fonts that have a
# line gap of their own. "fi fl" means Pages joins fi and fl into
# ligatures, and no others, as in Times and Palatino, which have only those
# two (Courier, fixed in width, has none); "fi fl ff ffi" adds ff and ffi,
# as in Helvetica Neue and its bold; "none" means it joins nothing.
# "spacing", when given, is added between letters, in ems: the free font
# that stands for the family has the widths of another (Helvetica for
# Helvetica Neue), and the spacing brings a line of text to the width it
# has in Pages. Regular and Light, the faces of body text, were measured
# on the text of a real document of 62 pages; the others on the sentence
# "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog 0123456789" at 12 pt.
# A family followed by UltraLight, Light, Medium or Bold is the face of
# that weight (100, 300, 500, 700 and over), where it lays out otherwise
# than the family. Pages rounds the ascent, the descent and the leading of
# each line to whole points. data/fonts/README.md explains.
